content.text:
I fixed it, but I couldn't run the type-check: TypeScript isn't installed locally, and the sandbox blocked downloading it. I also haven't tested a real meeting.

**What was wrong:** The app only reset the meeting's start time when it launched or when the previous meeting ended, not when you clicked Start. Any time the app sat open before your meeting was added to its length. That's how a 10-minute meeting came out as 100:00: about 90 minutes of waiting plus the 10 minutes of the meeting.

**The fix:**
- `electron/SessionTracker.ts`: added `markSessionStart()`, which resets the start time to now.
- `electron/IntelligenceManager.ts`: added a small wrapper that calls it.
- `electron/main.ts`: `startMeeting()` now calls it right when the meeting becomes active.

**A smaller bug in the same code:** in `electron/MeetingPersistence.ts`, the seconds were rounded up, so a meeting of 9:59.6 would have shown as "9:60". They're now rounded down, the same way the database already formats them.

Meetings already in your history keep their wrong lengths, because the bad value was saved when they ended. Only new meetings will be correct. To check, run `npx tsc --noEmit -p electron/tsconfig.json` once dependencies are installed, then do a short meeting after the app has been open a while and confirm the history shows the right length.

status_detail: meeting start time now resets on Start; 100:00 bug fixed
